zephyr-client-fixed.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_fixed.conf with the idle wait and batching off (main stack 9216 bytes), its node wz_session_mcu::slot_node
zephyr-client-fixed.chain_misses: calls through a register (9 on the path of the chain), which the stack gate's reader does not follow; the firmware's own reading is 424 bytes over the chain, since the initial sequence number stopped taking the permutation's frame (CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT) and the connect manager's planner call became a trait object, and the path that sets the reading was not identified
zephyr-client-fixed.measured: 2026-10-23, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd on the bench host; the stack line is the same in 7 of 7 runs, the GET figure is the median of 14 medians (0.320 to 0.471 ms) of 2000 queries for each of the node's two documents. The stack figures were re-read on 2026-10-27 after the not-a-Frame dispatch was split into decode, judge and engine steps (static chain 6,940, peak 6,060 in 2 of 2 runs, GETs inside their row; the tree before the split read 7,152 and 6,336, and the one before log_args 7,296 and 6,480): the decoded handshake message no longer sits in a frame under the engine's answer, and the worst chain is now the connect manager's dial path. After the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 the same build read static chain 6,372 and peak 5,880 in 2 of 2 runs (the engine's microstep buffers are sized to each document's state tree). On 2026-10-28 the five declarations a session with no allocator sends went through one dispatch, taking the arguments of their writer in place of a closure each (text 176,352 to 174,100 bytes): the worst chain reads 6,396 and the peak 5,904 in 1 of 1 run, 24 bytes over the row, 16 of them the enum the main frame now holds. On 2026-10-28 the initial sequence number became a compact function of the two zids (`CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT`, which this image's overlay turns on): the Keccak permutation was the deepest frame of the chain, which fell 500 bytes to 5,896 (17 frames, 12 calls through a register not followed), and the kit's reading did not move, 5,904 in 1 of 1 run, GETs answered by a zenohd with the new origin. On 2026-10-28 the connect manager's `drive` and `ask` took the planner's call as a trait object (one copy each and not one per closure): the chain fell to 5,512 (the main frame 1,792 to 1,256) and the peak read 5,904 as before, in 1 of 1 run

zephyr-client-fixed-batching.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_batching.conf with one send window sent as one datagram, the idle wait off (main stack 10240 bytes), its node wz_session_mcu::slot_node
zephyr-client-fixed-batching.chain_misses: calls through a register (9 on the path of the chain), which the stack gate's reader does not follow; the firmware's own reading is 428 bytes over the chain, since the initial sequence number stopped taking the permutation's frame (CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT) and the connect manager's planner call became a trait object, and the path that sets the reading was not identified
zephyr-client-fixed-batching.measured: 2026-10-23, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd on the bench host; the stack line is the same in 3 of 3 runs, the GET figure is the median of 6 medians (0.287 to 0.462 ms) of 2000 queries for each of the node's two documents. The two stack figures were re-measured on 2026-10-27 (static chain 7460, peak 6328 in 3 of 3 runs) and moved from 7204 and 6016: the slot node keeps the latest sample of a subscription (chain +136) and holds sessions a peer opened beside the dialled ones (+64), the connect manager is held by the shared planner and by nodes' zids (+88), a few smaller steps, and the log lines are no longer inlined into the main frame (-144); on 2026-10-27 the not-a-Frame dispatch was split into decode, judge and engine steps and the two read 6940 and 6060 in 2 of 2 runs (the worst chain is now the connect manager's dial path); after the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 they read 6372 and 5904 in 2 of 2 runs; on 2026-10-28 the five declarations a session with no allocator sends went through one dispatch (this image's text is 178,652 bytes after it) and the peak reads 5,928 in 1 of 1 run; the GET figure was not re-measured. On 2026-10-28 the initial sequence number became a compact function of the two zids (see the fixed client's row): the chain fell to 5,904 and the peak did not move, 5,928 in 1 of 1 run. The connect manager's planner call then became a trait object (see the fixed client's row): the chain 5,520 and the peak 5,908 in 3 of 3 runs (the first read a GET median of 492 us, outside the row, and the two runs after it did not)

zephyr-client-fixed-get.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_get.conf, which also asks one query at a time (two pending rows), the idle wait and batching off (main stack 12288 bytes); its node is wz_session_mcu::slot_node and its getter wz_session_mcu::slot_getter
zephyr-client-fixed-get.chain_misses: the reply sink and the reply view are called through a register (11 such calls on the path of the chain), which the stack gate's reader does not follow; the firmware's own reading is 344 bytes over the chain
zephyr-client-fixed-get.measured: 2026-10-23, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) asking a responder on the bench host, a client of a zenohd there, for a document of 165 bytes, 2050 queries with 50 of warm-up; the stack line and the getter's median (300 us, p99 1300 to 1400 us) are the same in 8 of 8 clean runs; the kernel tick is 100 us, so the median has that resolution. The two stack figures were re-measured on 2026-10-27 (static chain 7784, peak 8328 in 3 of 3 runs) and moved from 7672 and 8144; the changes on this path since 2026-10-23 are those named in the batching row, and this image's own share of them was not bisected; the same day the not-a-Frame dispatch was split into decode, judge and engine steps and the two read 7092 and 6648 in 2 of 2 runs (the reading was under the chain, so the `chain_misses` key was gone for that build); after the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 the chain reads 6524 and the reading is the same 6648 in 2 of 2 runs, so the reading is 124 bytes over the chain again and `chain_misses` is back. The chain fell 568 and the reading did not move, so the path that sets this peak is not the one the pin shortened; which it is was not found, and the calls through a register on the path (10) are where the reader stops; the getter's median was not re-measured; after the numbers and the console lines were written without core::fmt (the image's text is 185,432 bytes at that point and 185,768 with the polling path in the ITCM) the chain reads 6492 and the reading 6600 in 2 of 2 runs, 48 bytes lower, so the reading is 108 bytes over the chain; the getter's median was not re-measured. On 2026-10-28 the connect manager's planner call became a trait object: the chain reads 5,768 and the reading 6,160 in 1 of 1 run, 440 bytes lower, and the getter's median stayed inside its row. On 2026-10-28 the session's link driver was named by its type: the chain stayed 5,768 and the reading fell 48 bytes to 6,112 in 1 of 1 run, and the getter's median stayed inside its row. On 2026-10-28 the receive handed a lent record to its own callee and the getter asked only on the turn's own event: the chain stayed 5,768 and the reading fell 92 bytes to 6,020 in 1 of 1 run, the queries were asked and answered, and the getter's median stayed inside its row

zephyr-client-fixed-tls.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_tls.conf, which dials tls/ over Zephyr's TCP with the secure channel (wz-tls-mbedtls on Zephyr's Mbed TLS 4.1.0, mutual TLS 1.3, its 49,152-byte arena), the idle wait and batching off (main stack 12288 bytes), its node wz_session_mcu::slot_node
zephyr-client-fixed-tls.measured: 2026-10-24, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd 1.10.1 on the bench host that pins the image's certificate and is verified by it; the stack line is the same in 8 of 8 runs, the GET figure is the median of 8 medians (0.583 to 0.765 ms) of 2000 queries for each of the node's two documents; the client without the channel, run in turn with it, gave medians of 0.395 to 0.472 ms. The two stack figures were re-read on 2026-10-27 (static chain 7432 and peak 6752 in 2 of 2 runs, session established, peer verified) and moved from 7016 and 6864: the peak fell 112 with the split of the not-a-Frame dispatch into decode, judge and engine steps, and the chain, 7432 with and without that split, rose 416 with the connect manager's dial path since 2026-10-24, which was not bisected; after the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 the chain is the same 7432 and the peak reads 6688 in 2 of 2 runs; the GET figure was not re-measured
